_generated_by: manual (spiral_diff topology -- geometric free params + generator-derived electrical params)

n_turns.description: Number of turns PER ARM (each arm spirals inward from 'ct' to its own far terminus P1/P2) -- must be a positive multiple of 0.5 (each half-turn is one constant-radius 180-degree arc between two radius-step crossings, see inductor_spiral_diff_generator.py's diff_spiral_arms())

spacing_um.description: Edge-to-edge spacing between adjacent rings of the SAME arm

track_width_um.description: Metal5 winding trace width (also used for via4 sizing and the winding-adjacent Metal4 undercuts/jog miters -- NOT the P1/P2/ct port risers or the U port fixture, see 'port_track_width_um')

inner_diameter_um.description: Diameter of the open circle at the center of the winding (both arms' innermost ring stays outside this)

tab_length_um.description: Extra clearance between the outermost ring and the pad row baseline (added on top of the port routing's own natural clearance)

port_spacing_um.description: Half-spacing of the 3 pads (P1/P2/ct) from x=0 in the shared bottom pad row -- also the physical span the open/short-circuit-test port bridges in inductor_spiral_diff_generator.py's build_openems_structure()

port_track_width_um.description: 2026-09-22 (user decision): width of the port fixture's own Metal4 traces -- the P1/P2/ct risers AND the U-shaped port fixture (see build_openems_structure()'s own PORT_U_LEG_UM comment) -- independent of track_width_um. Metal4 is 2.25x more resistive per square than Metal5 in this stack (checked against gf180mcu_stack.json's own tt sheet-resistance values), and widening these traces costs nothing in r_outer/domain size (unlike widening the winding's own track_width_um), so this stays a separate, generously-sized knob. Must leave enough room for the port gap between the two U legs given port_spacing_um -- build_openems_structure() raises ValueError otherwise.

l.description: Self-inductance of each arm (ct to its own far terminus) -- fitted from a real 3-run open/short-circuit-test EM characterization when available (see tools/gf180mcu_spiral_diff_mutual_fit.py, NOT this topology's own generator's fit_electrical_params(), which only ever sees ONE run at a time -- see that function's own docstring), otherwise a generic placeholder literal. Substituted into BOTH L1 (arm A) and L2 (arm B) -- the mirror-construction winding makes La/Lb very close by design, any small measured difference is averaged rather than modeled as an asymmetry.

rs.description: Series winding resistance of each arm, same fit/placeholder split and same L1/L2-shared-value convention as 'l'.

cox.description: Oxide/substrate coupling capacitance at each OUTER terminal (P1, P2) -- real geometry x GF180MCU Metal5 area AND perimeter (fringe) capacitance data, always computed for real (no FDTD needed), summed over BOTH arms' own trace lengths. 1/4 of the total (trapezoidal 3-tap split: each outer terminal 1/4, 'ct' 1/2 -- see 'cox_ct').

rsub.description: Substrate spreading-loss resistance completing each outer terminal's oxide-coupling path -- real geometry-based estimate (GF180MCU isolation-substrate sheet resistance x trace area share) as a fallback; not independently EM-fittable by this topology's own generator's fit_electrical_params() (a single open/short-circuit-test run's Y11 doesn't correspond to the a<->b one-port measurement the staged rsub/csub fit assumes -- see that function's own docstring), so this stays at its geometry-based estimate until a dedicated fit against the 3-run data is developed.

csub.description: Substrate capacitance in parallel with rsub at each outer terminal -- placeholder-quality fallback, same not-yet-EM-fittable-by-this-topology caveat as 'rsub'.

cs.description: Coupling capacitance from each terminal to the center tap (ct) -- placeholder-quality constant, same convention as the 'spiral' topology (adjacent-turn crossover coupling is physically real for this multi-turn octagonal winding, unlike 'loop').

cox_ct.description: Oxide/substrate coupling capacitance at the center tap (ct) -- real geometry-based estimate, same quality as 'cox' (1/2 of the total, vs 1/4 at each outer terminal).

rsub_ct.description: Substrate spreading-loss resistance at the center tap -- real geometry-based estimate, same formula family as 'rsub' (half the value, matching cox_ct's double area share).

csub_ct.description: Substrate capacitance at the center tap -- propagated from 'csub' by the same 2x area ratio as cox_ct/rsub_ct, same as 'loop'/'spiral'. NOT independently observable from any of the 3 open/short-circuit-test runs (none of them drive 'sub' or float it the way the a<->b one-port measurement does), so this is purely a geometric propagation, never EM-fit.

rp_eddy.description: Resistance of the eddy-current/skin-proximity loss branch (Rp_eddy1/Rp_eddy2, in series with lp_eddy, in PARALLEL with each arm's own L1/L2) -- same ordinary (no mutual inductance) T-equivalent representation as 'loop'/'spiral' use for this SEPARATE physical mechanism (electrostatic Cox/Rsub/Csub is a different one). Set to a huge value (1e9 ohm) until a real EM fit against this topology's own 3-run data exists.

lp_eddy.description: Inductance of the eddy-current/skin-proximity loss branch -- see 'rp_eddy'. Irrelevant while rp_eddy is huge (placeholder path).

k_coupling.description: SPICE K mutual-coupling coefficient between L1 (arm A) and L2 (arm B) -- NEW for this topology (see inductor_spiral_diff.sch's own header comment): unlike 'loop'/'spiral', whose single continuous winding has no second, magnetically distinct arm, 'spiral_diff' is a genuine Y-branch of two separately-wound arms sharing node 'ct', so real magnetic coupling between them is physically meaningful. Fixed at 0.0 (no coupling assumed) until a real 3-run open/short-circuit-test EM characterization (tools/gf180mcu_spiral_diff_mutual_fit.py, via pi_model_fit.fit_mutual_inductance()) produces a measured k=m/sqrt(la*lb).
